doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Learning to arrange by copying records
summary: He taught himself arranging by transcribing records, including Lunceford reed choruses.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you learn your arranging skills?

Well actually I did a lot of studying for the arranging although I was doing a lot of writing when I was about 15 or 16, I used to take a lot of things off the record. I guess that was training, hearing instead of seeing what the parts looked like, and analyzing it from that see? So that helped a lot too.
I guess so. That’s quite an ear exercise to sit with a record and try to write down the parts.
Yeah, I used to do Jimmy Lunceford’s stuff when they had reed choruses. It was very difficult, so I had to wear out a few records to hear it.
